---
title: "Technical details"
---

altdown doesn't render anything itself:
[altdoc](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/) converts the man pages and vignettes
and renders them with Quarto, and altdown supplies the
[pkgdown](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/)-style layout around them.

## How a build works

`altdown::build_site()` runs in three stages:

1. **Before rendering**, it writes a set of files into `altdoc/`, which altdoc
   copies into its Quarto project. This is the approach altdoc
   [recommends](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/#/vignettes/customize) for
   customizing Quarto sites.
2. **During rendering**, `altdoc::render_docs()` converts the Rd files to Quarto
   pages and renders the project, with a pre-render script fixing up the man
   pages.
3. **After rendering**, it adds hover tooltips to the HTML in `docs/`.

The only file you edit is `altdoc/altdown.yml`. Everything else in `altdoc/` is
rewritten on every build, and gitignored by `altdown::use_altdown()`:

```text
altdoc/
├── altdown.yml                # configuration, edited by hand
├── quarto_website.yml         # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                   # home page
├── reference.qmd              # function reference index
├── authors.qmd                # authors and citation page
├── altdown.scss               # pkgdown-style theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── altdown-header.html        # dark-mode default
├── altdown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment
├── altdown-pre-render.R       # fixes up altdoc's man pages
└── altdown-rd-sections.rds    # man page sections altdoc gets wrong
```

## Before rendering

### The home page

`altdoc/index.md` replaces altdoc's home page. It holds the README next to a
pkgdown-style sidebar with links, the license, the citation, the developers and
the README's badges. On narrow screens the sidebar moves below the content.

A README `<picture>` with a light and a dark version (GitHub's
`prefers-color-scheme` convention) becomes one `<img>` per theme, switched by
the site's light/dark toggle.

### The reference index

altdoc can't group and order the function index
([etiennebacher/altdoc#326](https://github.com/etiennebacher/altdoc/issues/326)),
so `altdoc/altdown.yml` has a `reference:` field in the same shape as pkgdown's:

```yaml
reference:
  - title: Building the site       # <1>
    desc: >                        # <2>
      Set up a package, then build its site.
    contents:
      - use_altdown                # <3>
      - starts_with("build_")      # <4>
```

1. Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.
2. An optional description, shown under the heading.
3. A topic, by any of its `\alias{}` names.
4. A selector, as in pkgdown: `starts_with()`, `ends_with()`, `contains()`,
   `matches()`, `has_concept()`, `has_keyword()`, `-` to exclude and `c()` to
   combine.

### The navbar and footer

The navbar links the "Get started" vignette, the reference index, the other
vignettes under "Articles" and the changelog. The footer has pkgdown's
"Developed by ..." text, built from `Authors@R`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Changing the Quarto configuration

A `quarto:` field in `altdown.yml` is merged over the generated configuration.
Lists, like the navbar's items, are appended to; any other setting is replaced,
and `~` removes it. For example, to add a navbar link and fold code blocks:

```yaml
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true
```
:::

## During rendering: the man pages

altdoc converts `man/*.Rd` to `.qmd` and renders straight after, so
`build_site()` can't edit those pages beforehand. Instead,
`altdown-pre-render.R` runs as a Quarto pre-render script and makes them look
like pkgdown's:

- **Usage** is a syntax-highlighted R code block with a copy button.
- **Inline code** is rendered as Markdown code spans, so quotes and backslashes
  survive Pandoc.
- **Examples** show their output in the same block, prefixed with `#>`, and the
  `library()` call for the package itself is hidden.
- **`\dontrun{}` examples** become plain code blocks, so the page renders
  without starting an R session.
- **Rd macros** work: altdoc ignores the package's own Rd macros (`RdMacros:` in
  `DESCRIPTION`, or `man/macros/`), so Rdpack's `\insertRef{}`, for instance,
  shows its raw arguments. `build_site()` renders those Rd files again with
  them, and the script swaps in the sections that differ.
- **A custom `\section{Examples}{}`** (prose rather than `\examples{}`) stays
  prose: altdoc would wrap it in an R chunk, which fails to run.

## After rendering: hover tooltips

After rendering, `build_site()` links every reference to one of the package's
functions, in code blocks or inline code, to its man page. Hovering shows a
tooltip with its usage and the first sentence of its description. Try it: hover
over `build_site()` or `use_altdown()`.

The sentence is cut off at 200 characters, and `build_site()` warns when one is
longer. To build without tooltips, use `build_site(tooltips = FALSE)`.

## Matching the pkgdown look

`altdown.scss` is styled after pkgdown's `pkgdown.scss`, written for Quarto's
HTML, and layered on top of Quarto's own themes:

```yaml
theme:
  light: [default, altdown.scss]
  dark: [darkly, altdown.scss]
```

`darkly` normally uses the Lato web font and larger headings, so text would
reflow when toggling between light and dark. `altdown.scss` therefore sets
Bootstrap's system font stack and heading sizes for both themes.

Two things need JavaScript:

- **Dark mode by default.** `altdown-header.html` starts new visitors on the
  dark theme if their system prefers it.
- **Aligning the navbar title with the body text.** The body's left edge differs
  between the home page and other pages, so `altdown-after-body.html` measures
  it and adjusts the navbar's padding.
